title: No auxiliary entry targets a still-free variable
statement: Let $t$ be a term on $n$ variables (a list of literals), let $L$ be a list of literals each paired with a natural-number position, let $\pi$ be a path (a list of variable–direction pairs), and let $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$ be restrictions on $n$ variables. Suppose every pair in $L$ occurs in the indexed enumeration of $t$, so that each $(l,i)\in L$ records a literal $l$ sitting at position $i$ of $t$. Run the clause-processing procedure that consumes the free literals of $L$ against $\pi$ starting from $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$, and let $\rho_0'$ denote its updated $\rho_0$-restriction and $A$ its list of clause auxiliary entries. If $\rho_0'$ leaves the variable $v$ free, then for every entry $(i,d)\in A$ and every literal $l$ such that deleting the first $i$ literals of $t$ leaves a nonempty list with head $l$, the variable of $l$ is not $v$.
hypotheses_covered: t is a term on n variables (a list of literals)
L is a list of literals each paired with a natural-number position
pi is a path: a list of variable-direction pairs
rho_0 and sigma are restrictions on n variables
every pair in L occurs in the indexed enumeration of t
the updated rho_0-restriction produced by the procedure leaves v free
replaced:
Assuming every literal in $\mathit{lits}$ is an indexed literal of the term $t$, if the
restriction component $(\mathrm{processClauseLits}\ \mathit{lits}\ \mathit{path}\ \rho_0\ \sigma).2.1$
is unset at $v$, then no auxiliary entry produced by the fold targets $v$: for every aux
entry $e$, dropping $e.1$ literals of $t$ to a head literal $l$ gives $l.\mathrm{var} \neq v$.
